LESSON: WRITING 12.4.1 PARAGRAPHS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Writing 12.4.1 Paragraphs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 12.4.1 Paragraphs, part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to put sentences in the correct order when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 12.4.1 Paragraphs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to write clearly and correctly is developed as they write the sentences sequentially to form a

paragraph.

Values:
Responsibility is inculcated as the learner takes up the initiative to write sentences sequentially to form paragraphs.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life-skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s esteem is enhanced as their writing skills improve.

95

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner applies the writing skills to writing of paragraphs in Kiswahili and indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,

• Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

• Pictures or picture description
